findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the filled blue 'Write to me' block and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one personal action looks like a button and a link, but neither does anything. 'Write to me' is a static box with a hover rule (p11, p12). The underlined address is static text, not a mailto link (p13). The only working mailto is in the footer, at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who decides to contact Mark from the hero clicks the button or the address and nothing happens. The one thing the page exists for fails at the moment they act, and the brief makes this route the test the tile must pass.

findings.where: First screen, 'Book a consultation': a second filled blue button set beside 'Write to me' at equal weight (desktop), and on its own indented line out of alignment with 'Write to me' (phone)
findings.fault: The hero has two primary actions in the same strongest colour and fill, so neither leads. The second offers a booking route Mark has not chosen. It links to #consult, and no consultation section appears anywhere on the page. On the phone it starts about 16 px to the right of the button above it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark, and the brand sheet leaves a booking link to the owner. A visitor also has to choose between two equal buttons, and the booking one leads nowhere.

findings.where: First screen, the hero ground: a pale blue-to-lilac gradient band behind the heading, notes, photo and actions, under a paper-coloured header strip
findings.fault: The hero sits on a cool blue-violet gradient, not on the warm paper. Lilac is not a house colour. The page's own palette section says 'Three colours, no accent' and 'No texture: the paper is a flat warm tone'. The first screen breaks the system the rest of the page declares, and the gradient gives it a stock tech-landing look.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first. The brief asks for a warm paper ground with the house blue and grey as the only ink, warns against slick looks and anything that reads as 'techy', and says a tile fails on a look any consultancy could own.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph 'I advise multilateral development banks…' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's own sentence about what he does is set in bold, widely tracked, all-caps sans over four lines (eight on the phone). The next paragraph of the same voice is in the body serif. The most important plain statement on the page reads like a shouted label and is the hardest text in the hero to read. It also contradicts the type specimen, which gives the sans only to 'notes and labels'.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader doing the 5-second scan for 'what does he do, for whom' has to work through a block of caps. The founder would object because the brief bans tracked techy capitals and asks for Mark's voice in a serif text column.

findings.where: Margin notes beside the hero (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024, each with a talk title), and the blue section labels in the left margin below the fold (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: These are static text in the house blue, which the palette names as the link colour. The hero notes even carry talk titles, which a visitor expects to open the talk. None of them acts (p5–p10, p15–p26, p48–p49), so they look like links but go nowhere. The brief asks for blue margin notes, so this conflicts with the brief's own look and needs the founder's ruling.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to see Mark's Istanbul or São Paulo talk clicks the title and nothing happens. That costs trust right where the page offers its proof of work.

findings.where: Header: the MMM Infra mark and its 'MMM INFRA' wordmark (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The lockup's wordmark sits on the seam between the paper header strip and the gradient hero, with its baseline touching the band edge. The logo looks cropped by the hero, not placed with clear space around it.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark. The logo is the one fixed brand asset, and it reads as if it was squeezed in at its most visible point.

findings.where: Navigation: Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog
findings.fault: The nav links point to #profile, #articles and #blog, and none of those sections exists on the page. There is no Contact item in the nav either, so the nav offers three routes that do nothing visible and none to the action the page is for.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who uses the nav to find Mark's publications, the proof an advisor's buyers look for, finds that the page doesn't move.

findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF row's 'Download' button, against the hero's buttons
findings.fault: The download action is an outlined capsule with an icon. The hero's actions are square-cornered filled rectangles. Two button shapes on one page give the actions no shared look, and the capsule makes the minor action look like a standout.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and any later page builder, who get no single button pattern to reuse. A careful reader also notices that the page's parts do not belong to one family.

findings.where: Hero exhibit photograph and the motion sketch's exhibit photograph
findings.fault: The photograph has a wide, soft, lilac-tinted drop shadow at rest. That shadow suggests the photo floats or can be acted on, but it is static. It is also the only shadow on the page, and it reads as a generic card lift rather than a framed exhibit with a mount or edge.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief asks for real items framed as objects, and a floating shadow is a stock web effect, not a frame.

findings.fault: The italic serif caption and the sans 'Placeholder' note run on as one wrapped line in two faces and sizes. The second line falls with uneven leading, so the caption looks broken rather than set.
findings.who_objects: Angélique's articles will carry captions on every image, and this is the specimen she copies. A reader sees a ragged, two-font caption under every photo.

findings.where: Motion sketch (desktop): the curve on the left, and the photo and table on the far right
findings.fault: The curve and its caption end high on the left, which leaves a large empty block beside the table. The exhibit photo floats alone at the right edge, apart from its own heading. The section breaks up into scattered pieces where the rest of the page keeps to its text column.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen as a showcase of the tile's calm, ordered layout, sees the one section that looks unfinished.
